answer: Cross-Context Attestation Ledger: each identity must publish signed answers to randomly drawn tasks, and peers log those answers in a shared ledger keyed to the response content. A clone reusing its origin's answers trips matching-content flags; divergent answers reveal the split at the nadir of consensus scoring. Honest agents pay only signing and storage. An attacker must fund distinct, consistent work histories per clone—cost scaling linearly, since a shared haven of cached answers collapses under content hashing. Ledger checks leave no safe mesa for silent duplication.
